## Hi, I'm Josh

I'm a third year Ph.D. candidate in the
[Department of Statistical Science](https://stat.duke.edu) at Duke University, working with
Jerry Reiter and Fan Li.

My research sits at the intersection of **causal inference** and **missing data**.
Specifically, I seek to develop Bayesian methodology that can estimate heterogeneous treatment
effects in the presence of missing data.

Before Duke I graduated summa cum laude from UCLA in 2024 with a B.S. in Applied Mathematics,
Statistics and Data Science. Alongside my methods work I collaborate as a biostatistician with
Duke, UC San Diego, and previously Stanford University Schools of Medicine.

I am highly passionate about teaching. In Summer 2026 I was instructor of record for
[STA 199L: Introduction to Data Science and Statistical Thinking](https://sta199-su26-2.github.io/).

Outside the department you'll find me on the court with Duke Men's Club Volleyball, performing
with Duke Chinese Dance, flipping with Duke Gymnastics, or loudly defending UCLA sports deep in
ACC country.
